> I will be making a car parking simulator using cardboard and other electronics. Once a car arrives at the barrier, there will be an ultrasonic sensor that will tell what sort of vehicle is entering the parking. This could be anything from a normal car all the way to a massive lorry. Once the sensor recognizes, what sort of vehicle it is, the barrier will open and  there will be a small IPS screen that will show you where to go (left, right, straight ahead).

### 2026-10-04 — Built from durable recycled cardboard, this interactive parking simulator demonstrates automated traffic management and smart-city logistics using integrated microelectronics. The setup features a mai

**4.88h**

Built from durable recycled cardboard, this interactive parking simulator demonstrates automated traffic management and smart-city logistics using integrated microelectronics. The setup features a main driving platform measuring $50\text{ cm} \times 40\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm}$ $(\text{Length} \times \text{Width} \times \text{Height})$ alongside a dedicated entry kiosk and barrier tower measuring $15\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm} \times 25\text{ cm}$. When an incoming vehicle reaches the gate, an ultrasonic sensor scans its size profile to classify the transport—distinguishing everything from compact passenger cars to heavy long-haul lorries. Upon successful identification, a motorized servo arm lifts the cardboard barrier gate, and an integrated IPS LCD screen immediately displays dynamic directional guidance (instructing the driver to head left, right, or straight ahead toward an appropriately sized bay). Combining accessible cardboard infrastructure with practical sensor integration, this scale model provides an engaging, hands-on demonstration of modern automated parking systems. I have got inspiration from images and will implement them in my final project
